LMP3.title: Eurointernational wins LMP3 after Falb’s late puncture
LMP3.dek: Mondini and van Berlo won for Eurointernational after the leading United Ligier of Falb and Rayhall picked up a puncture late on; 360 Racing took second and United’s #3 third.

facts.v: Lahaye’s 1:45.386 gave Ultimate its first ELMS pole, and his first since the 2012 Donington round.

facts.t: Puncture ten minutes from the end
facts.v: John Falb’s #2 pulled off with a right-rear puncture after contact with an IDEC LMP2 Ligier, handing the lead to Eurointernational.

chapters.title: A bigger field and a Norma sweep
text: LMP3 came to Monza with more cars than at Le Castellet, where RLR MSport’s Ligier had won the opener. Racing for Poland made a one-off ELMS debut with a Ligier for Enqvist, Blicharski and Fontana, Jensen returned to the AT Racing Ligier #9, and Still took the seat in Inter Europol’s #14 that Enqvist had filled as a late call-up in France.

United Autosports arrived as defending class champions, but Wells crashed the #3 in Wednesday’s test. The car was repaired in time for the weekend. In first practice the Normas filled the top three: Oregon Team’s #10 was quickest on 1:46.136, despite stopping at the first chicane under a full-course yellow before restarting, ahead of M. Racing-YMR’s #19 and Ultimate’s #17. United’s #2 was the best Ligier in fourth. The #19 led second practice on 1:46.623, with the AT Racing Ligier second and the #17 third.

chapters.title: Lahaye’s last-lap pole
text: Lahaye took pole for Ultimate on 1:45.386, improving on his final lap to beat the time Droux had set in the M. Racing-YMR Norma #19 by two tenths. It was the team’s first pole and the second in a row for the Norma M30. Jensen’s AT Racing Ligier was third, only five thousandths behind the #19 and the best of the Ligiers, with Rayhall fourth in the United #2 and van Uitert fifth for RLR. Lahaye called the car perfect.

Scrutineering changed the class grid. The AT Racing Ligier #9 had all its qualifying times cancelled because its front splitter was below the regulation height, and it was sent to the back of the class. That moved the United #2 up to third on the revised grid and RLR’s #15 to fourth. Eurointernational’s #11 had qualified sixth in class on 1:46.161 and began from the same position.

chapters.title: The Norma leads, then trouble
text: Ultimate’s #17 led from pole in the opening hour but soon ran into trouble. Heriau was nearly forced off the track at Turn 4 by Racing for Poland’s #20, which was later shown the black-and-orange flag for a loose piece of rear bodywork. Safety cars for an LMP2 crash at the second Lesmo and then an off at Ascari kept bunching the field.

chapters.title: Three cars, one strategy
text: With the Norma out of the lead, three Ligiers on identical pit strategies became the contenders: United’s #2, Eurointernational’s #11 and Inter Europol’s #13. They ran nose to tail through the final hour, and the #2 took the lead after its last stop.

The fourth and last safety car of the race followed a lengthy clean-up at the exit of the second Lesmo, where the AT Racing #9 hit the stranded M. Racing-YMR Ligier #18. Neither car was classified, and DKR Engineering’s Norma #8 was also among the class’s non-classified finishers after 46 laps.

chapters.title: Falb pulls off, van Berlo takes over
text: Ten minutes from the flag the race turned. Falb’s #2 had brief side-to-side contact with an IDEC Sport LMP2 Ligier at Turn 1 and then pulled off with a right-rear puncture, ending the defending champions’ hopes of a first win of the year. Van Berlo inherited the lead for Eurointernational.

He was then pressed by Hippe in the Inter Europol #13, two seconds behind, until the Ligier needed fuel in the closing laps. That opened second and third to Kaiser and Woodward in 360 Racing’s #6 and to United’s #3.

chapters.title: Eurointernational’s second ELMS win
text: Mondini and van Berlo’s #11 won on 118 laps, the second ELMS LMP3 victory for both Eurointernational and Mondini and the sixth in a row for the Ligier JS P3. Woodward, Kaiser and Swift were second in 360 Racing’s #6, one lap down, with Wells, Grist and Bell third in United’s #3. Inter Europol’s #13 was fourth, Falb and Rayhall’s #2 recovered to fifth, and NEFIS by Speed Factory’s #5 was sixth, all on 117 laps.

Pole-sitter Ultimate finished seventh in class on 116 laps, ahead of Oregon Team’s #10, and Lahaye set the class fastest lap, 1:47.651. The #18, #9 and #8 were not classified. The series next heads to the Red Bull Ring on 22 July.

LMGTE.title: Spirit of Race wins GTE after leading most of the way
LMGTE.dek: Cameron, Griffin and Scott won for Spirit of Race from third on the class grid, ahead of Proton’s #77 Porsche and the Ebimotors Porsche that took pole.

facts.v: Pera’s 1:47.493 put the Ebimotors Porsche on pole at its home race, 0.018s clear of Bruni’s Proton Porsche.

chapters.title: Six cars and two guest Porsche drivers
text: Six GTE cars lined up at Monza, two fewer than at Le Castellet, with no FIA WEC guest entries this time. The clash with the Nürburgring 24 Hours reshaped Proton Competition’s two Porsche 911 RSRs: Lieb, the 2011 GTE-Pro champion, joined Ried and Dienst in the #77, and Bruni, making his first ELMS start since 2012, joined the Roda pair in the #88. The Ebimotors Porsche #80 was the car that had run at Spa the weekend before as a Dempsey-Proton entry in the WEC.

Proton’s #88 topped first practice on 1:48.457, ahead of Krohn Racing’s #83 and JMW’s #66, where Molina set the third-fastest time. Griffin was quickest for Spirit of Race in the second session on 1:48.022, but JMW’s session ended when Liam Griffin locked the rears at Turn 4 and hit the wall head-on, causing a red flag of roughly ten minutes.

chapters.title: Pera takes a home pole
text: Riccardo Pera, an 18-year-old Italian, took pole for Ebimotors at the team’s home race with 1:47.493, narrowly holding off three platinum-rated rivals. Bruni’s Proton #88 was second, 0.018 seconds behind, and Matt Griffin put the Spirit of Race Ferrari third, 0.081 off pole as the best of the Ferraris. Bertolini’s Krohn Ferrari #83 was fourth and Lieb’s Proton #77 fifth.

JMW’s #66 did not take part. The Ferrari was still in the garage after the final-practice shunt, was repaired overnight and, with the stewards’ approval, started the race from the back of the grid with Molina as the starting driver.

chapters.title: Safety cars and a rear-of-grid start
text: The GTE cars started with JMW’s Ferrari at the back and Spirit of Race third on the class grid. An early crash for an LMP2 Oreca at the second Lesmo, about 15 minutes in, brought the first of the safety cars, and another followed when a G-Drive Oreca went off at Ascari just before the end of the hour.

chapters.title: Spirit of Race take control
text: Spirit of Race held the class lead for most of the race and dominated the final two hours. Proton’s #77 ran second and was one of the few Porsches to have a clean day, and Ebimotors’ #80 completed the podium. JMW’s Ferrari recovered from the back of the grid to finish fourth in class.

chapters.title: A minute in hand
text: Cameron, Griffin and Scott took the Spirit of Race Ferrari home to win by about a minute from Ried, Dienst and Lieb in Proton’s #77. Pera’s pole-winning Ebimotors Porsche completed the podium with Babini and Narac.

chapters.title: Spirit of Race’s win, Ebimotors on the podium
text: The #55 Spirit of Race Ferrari won on 116 laps, with the #77 Proton Porsche second and the #80 Ebimotors Porsche third on the same lap. JMW’s #66 was fourth on 115 laps from last on the grid, Proton’s #88 with Bruni was fifth, and Krohn Racing’s #83 sixth on 114. All six cars were classified, and Pera set the class fastest lap, 1:49.042.
Bruni and Lieb’s one-off Proton appearances ended there, and the series next heads to the Red Bull Ring on 22 July.
